assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, central appetite effects) led to incretin-based drugs that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and clinical impact are exceptional, spanning basic physiology to therapy.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of the active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (biology and therapeutic development) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis) are the most defensible trio from the credited names. Knudsen's industrial development of the long-acting analogues is real but is the most dispensable for a three-person limit. Credit disputes over early GLP-1 work remain.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably pressing given global impact.
uncertainties: Priority of the early GLP-1 identification work is contested and I have not independently verified the record.
Whether the committee would favour physiology over drug development is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience millisecond-precision, cell-type-specific control of activity and became a standard tool for dissecting circuits, including motor and locomotor circuits, behaviour and disease models. The enabling idea and its microbial-opsin basis are original and the impact across neuroscience is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth; Miesenböck's earlier genetic light-control concept) are all decisive. With a three-name limit I favour Deisseroth with the two channelrhodopsin discoverers, leaving out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, which is a real unresolved allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely replicated and used for over fifteen years; the main open question is the clinical translation, which is nascent. A tool-based prize fits precedent.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited people is unresolved and any three-person selection is contestable.
Therapeutic translation is limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living drugs. The clinical and conceptual impact is clear, with approved products.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T with costimulation), Sadelain (second-generation costimulated CARs, preclinical foundations) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials) form a plausible trio. Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is not among the credited names, which weakens the attribution picture.
assessment.maturity: Approved therapies with years of follow-up; solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity management remain open, but the core discovery is established.
uncertainties: Absence of the original chimeric-receptor inventor in the credited names complicates fair attribution.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The demonstration that TNF is a dominant driver of chronic inflammation, and that its blockade controls rheumatoid arthritis, changed the treatment of many immune-mediated diseases. This is a clear bench-to-bedside discovery with enormous lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini's joint work from the cytokine-cascade concept to clinical trials is a clean two-person configuration. Contributions from antibody developers and others are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of clinical use and confirmation; it is arguably overdue and not premature.
uncertainties: Some may argue for including antibody-engineering contributors or other cytokine biologists.
The prize committee's past treatment of immunotherapy-adjacent work may affect priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR and mTORC1/2 define how cells couple nutrient and growth-factor signals to growth, metabolism and ageing, with implications for cancer, diabetes and immunity. The discovery is original and conceptually unifying.
assessment.attribution: Hall's identification of TOR in yeast is the foundational contribution; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and its regulators. Schreiber's work on rapamycin target binding is important chemical biology but I would leave it out of a two-person prize. Heitman and Hall's early yeast work is also relevant but not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across systems; clinical use of rapalogs is established, though broader translational promise is partly unrealised.
uncertainties: Credit split between the chemical-biology and the genetic-discovery arms is unresolved.
Some of Sabatini's later history may affect committee views, which I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HER2 amplification as a prognostic driver and trastuzumab as targeted therapy established a model of antibody-based, biomarker-selected cancer treatment with large survival gains.
assessment.attribution: Ullrich (HER2 cloning), Slamon (clinical association and trials) and Shepard (antibody development) correspond to distinct steps and fit a three-person prize. Others who identified the neu oncogene (e.g. Weinberg's group) are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Mature, extensively confirmed and practice-changing for decades.
uncertainties: Credit for the earlier neu oncogene discovery lies outside the supplied names.
Targeted oncology may be judged to have been partly recognised via earlier prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the principal cellular model of synaptic plasticity underlying learning and memory, and my own field of neural circuit physiology depends on its concepts. Its original observation and the later NMDA receptor mechanism are fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo reported the original phenomenon in 1973; Collingridge established NMDA receptor dependence. Morris's behavioural link to memory is also strong, so a three-person configuration necessarily excludes a significant contributor.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, though the causal link between LTP and memory remains debated.
uncertainties: The relationship of LTP to actual memory storage is not fully resolved.
Fair allocation among four credited names is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that correct SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which affects motor neurons. It is a mechanism-driven, strongly clinical advance in a devastating motor neuron disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) are the two credited names and form a coherent pair. Contributions from the SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with growing long-term data; relatively recent, so recognition might be slightly early compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Foundational SMN1 gene discovery is not among the credited names.
Long-term durability and the generalisability of the approach beyond SMA are still being established.
